    Add a structural $THETA (and optionally an IIV) to an established FREM model

    addFremStructuralTheta.Rd

    Inserts one new structural (non-FREM) $THETA at index numNonFREMThetas + 1, immediately before the FREM covariate-mean thetas. Every THETA() reference at or after that index is shifted up by one - in $THETA itself and in every record that can hold abbreviated code ($PK, $PRED, $ERROR, $DES, $AES, $MIX, $INFN), which in a FREM model is the MU_k = THETA(numNonFREMThetas + c) block - so the model stays consistent. numNonFREMThetas increases by one.

    With addEta = TRUE the function also adds a matching IIV via addFremIIV() and wires the two together. This is the usual entry point: adding a structural parameter with a typical value, an MU reference and between-subject variability in one step.

    Usage

    addFremStructuralTheta(
  strFREMModel,
  thetaInit,
  parameter = NULL,
  addEta = FALSE,
  muReference = TRUE,
  omegaInit = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  numNonFREMThetas = NULL,
  numSkipOm = NULL,
  extFile = NULL,
  newModel = NULL,
  bWriteMod = TRUE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

    Arguments

    strFREMModel

    Path to the FREM model file, or a character vector of its lines.

    thetaInit

    Initial value for the new $THETA. Required - a scalar (e.g. 0.1), a length-3 numeric c(low, init, up), or a string written verbatim after $THETA (e.g. "(0, 1.2)" or "0.5 FIX").

    parameter

    Name of the $PK variable the new theta belongs to. If it has no $PK assignment yet a definition is created for it; if it already exists, that assignment is modified in place. Required when addEta = TRUE; optional otherwise (with no parameter only the $THETA record is added and the caller wires it in by hand).

    addEta

    Logical. Also add an accompanying IIV (via addFremIIV())? Default FALSE.

    muReference

    Logical. Only used when addEta = TRUE - see Details. Default TRUE.

    omegaInit

    Initial variance for the new $OMEGA. Required when addEta = TRUE.

    label

    Comment for the new $THETA record. Defaults to "TV_<parameter>" or "added structural THETA".

    numNonFREMThetas, numSkipOm

    Structural integers. NULL (default) to derive them from the model + .ext; supply to override.

    extFile

    Path to the .ext for the derivation. Defaults to the model path with a .ext extension.

    newModel

    Output path when strFREMModel is a path and bWriteMod = TRUE. Defaults to the input path with _theta inserted before the extension.

    bWriteMod

    Logical. Write the new model? Default TRUE.

    quiet

    Logical. Suppress progress messages. Default TRUE.

    Value

    Invisibly, a list with

    model

    the new model as a character vector

    thetaIndex

    the index of the inserted $THETA

    etaIndex

    the index of the inserted ETA(), or NA when addEta = FALSE

    numNonFREMThetas

    the updated count, always one more than the input

    numSkipOm

    the skip count. Updated only when addEta = TRUE - with addEta = FALSE no random effect was added, so it comes back unchanged. Either way it is the right value to pass to the next call.

    file

    the path written, or NULL

    Details

    The existing .ext / .phi are not migrated - the model must be re-estimated. Only the control stream is rewritten.

    The new record is placed by counting the values in $THETA, expanding (value)xN repeats, so a record holding several values on one line is handled. When the insertion point falls inside such a line, the function stops and asks for that line to be split rather than guessing. A model with $ABBR REPLACE THETA(<label>)=THETA(<n>) is refused, since renumbering would leave the label pointing at the old index.

    Whether parameter already exists in $PK decides what happens:

    A new parameter (no $PK assignment) gets a definition inserted just before the FREM MU_k = THETA(...) block, delimited by ;; Begin added THETA / ;; End added THETA so it is visually separate from the FREM covariate block. With j = numNonFREMThetas + 1 (the new theta) and k = numSkipOm + 1 (the new eta):

    addEta = TRUE, muReference = TRUE

    TV<parameter> = THETA(<j>), MU_<k> = LOG(TV<parameter>), <parameter> = EXP(MU_<k> + ETA(<k>)) - log-normal and MU-referenced, the form the FREM models themselves use for CL / V / MAT.

    addEta = TRUE, muReference = FALSE

    <parameter> = THETA(<j>) * EXP(ETA(<k>)) (log-normal, no MU line).

    addEta = FALSE

    <parameter> = THETA(<j>) - a structural parameter with no between-subject variability.

    An existing parameter - matched without regard to case, in $PK or, in a model that has no $PK, in $PRED - is modified in place instead: its $PK assignment gains a * THETA(<j>) factor, and with addEta = TRUE also an * EXP(ETA(<k>)) term. Nothing is inserted, so no markers appear.

    The MU-referenced form deliberately goes through TV<parameter> rather than writing MU_<k> = THETA(<j>) directly. generateFremModel() locates the FREM block as everything from the first MU_<n> = THETA( line to the last COV<n> = MU_ line and regenerates it; a direct MU_<k> = THETA(<j>) here would match that pattern, and being before the FREM block would move the start of the replaced range - so a later updateFREMmodel() would silently delete this definition. The LOG(TV...) form cannot collide.

    Markers are only ever placed in $PK, never in $THETA / $OMEGA, where generateFremModel() reads comments positionally and a standalone comment line would shift every subsequent parameter label.

    See also

    addFremIIV(), updateFREMmodel()

    Other FREM model management: addFremIIV(), createFREMmodel(), updateFREMmodel()

    Examples

    # A structural THETA on a parameter run31.mod does not have yet, with a
# matching IIV. The .ext is not migrated: the model has to be re-estimated.
td <- tempfile()
dir.create(td)
file.copy(system.file("extdata/SimNeb/run31.mod", package = "PMXFrem"), td)
#> [1] TRUE
file.copy(system.file("extdata/SimNeb/run31.ext", package = "PMXFrem"), td)
#> [1] TRUE

res <- addFremStructuralTheta(file.path(td, "run31.mod"),
  thetaInit = 0.5, parameter = "KA2", addEta = TRUE, omegaInit = 0.04,
  bWriteMod = FALSE
)
res$thetaIndex # 8: just before the FREM covariate-mean thetas
#> [1] 8
res$etaIndex # 3: numSkipOm + 1
#> [1] 3

# the house form, so a later updateFREMmodel() does not splice it away
grep("KA2", res$model, value = TRUE)
#> [1] "     TVKA2 = THETA(8)"         "     MU_3 = LOG(TVKA2)"       
#> [3] "     KA2 = EXP(MU_3 + ETA(3))" "$THETA  0.5 ; 8. TV_KA2"      
#> [5] "$OMEGA  0.04  ; 3. IIV on KA2"

unlink(td, recursive = TRUE)
